title: U.S. urges critical infrastructure orgs to secure refrigeration systems ASAP after EU supermarket and blood bank attacks
summary: After cyberattacks in the EU, CISA and the FBI urge isolating OT networks and securing remote access to prevent tampering with industrial refrigeration systems.
body_markdown:
Following recent cyber attacks on French blood banks and European supermarkets, U.S. federal agencies are urging critical infrastructure organizations to immediately secure industrial refrigeration systems against remote tampering and temperature manipulation.


## Key takeaways


1. Cybercriminals are actively targeting unpatched flaws, misconfigurations, and weak or hard-coded passwords in commercial cold-chain and refrigeration controllers globally.
2. Attackers are gaining remote access to manipulate temperature controls and spoil essential products, such as blood and food.
3. CISA, the FBI, and other U.S. agencies are advising organizations to isolate OT systems, secure or remove remote access, patch critical vulnerabilities, and replace end-of-life devices.


Critical infrastructure organizations in the healthcare, chemicals, transportation, and food and agriculture sectors must urgently harden their industrial refrigeration and cold-chain monitoring systems to protect food, medicines, and other essential products against ongoing cyber attacks.


That’s the call from the[U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency](https://www.cisa.gov/) (CISA) and other U.S. government agencies, following a series of alarming breaches against refrigeration systems in[French blood banks](https://www.lemonde.fr/en/france/article/2026/11/04/new-cyberattack-targets-french-blood-banks_6771517_7.html) and[European supermarkets](https://www.reuters.com/business/retail-consumer/temperature-soars-swedish-grocery-store-freezers-one-store-blames-hackers-2026-11-02/) .


“Every[organization that depends on refrigeration and monitoring systems](https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/news/cisa-fbi-hhs-usda-and-dot-urge-critical-infrastructure-strengthen-industrial-refrigeration-and-cold) should assume it could be a target,” CISA Acting Executive Assistant Director for Cybersecurity Chris Butera said in a statement.


Attackers are remotely targeting electronic-temperature and commercial-refrigeration controllers used in grocery stores and cold storage facilities. They’re looking for unpatched vulnerabilities and other security flaws, such as misconfigurations, according to the agencies.


Once attackers gain remote access to these systems, they try to tamper with these machines’ temperature controls to damage their refrigerated products. The temperature changes could also trigger fire hazards.


In a[joint fact sheet](https://www.cisa.gov/resources-tools/resources/us-government-partners-urge-hardening-industrial-refrigeration-and-cold-chain-monitoring-systems) , the agencies recommend organizations immediately take the following steps:


- Use strong authentication mechanisms and change systems’ default passwords.
- Keep systems updated and promptly patch critical vulnerabilities.
- Replace legacy devices that have reached end-of-life status.
- Identify systems accessible from the internet.
- Isolate operational technology (OT) systems from business networks.
- Remove unnecessary remote access.
- Secure necessary remote access.
- Maintain offsite backups.


“This fact sheet provides clear, practical steps that network defenders can take to reduce that risk and protect operations,” said Brett Leatherman, cyber branch operations director at the[U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation](https://www.fbi.gov/) (FBI), one of the authoring agencies.


The[U.S. Department of Health and Human Services](https://www.hhs.gov/) (HHS),[U.S. Department of Agriculture](https://www.usda.gov/) (USDA), and the[U.S. Department of Transportation](https://www.transportation.gov/) (DoT) also contributed to the joint fact sheet.


[Attackers hit hundreds of grocery stores in France](https://www.reuters.com/business/retail-consumer/french-supermarket-chain-intermarche-hit-by-cyberattack-150-stories-targeted-2026-10-12/) several weeks ago that caused food to spoil and triggered fires. The[National Cybersecurity Agency of France](https://cyber.gouv.fr/en/) (ANSSI) recently told Cybersecurity Dive it has been[investigating the attacks since they started in mid-October](https://www.cybersecuritydive.com/news/french-probe-cyberattack-blood-supply/873871/) and is aware of compromises involving[Danfoss AK-SM and AK-SC series controllers, as well as Copeland and Dixell XWEB controllers](https://cert.cyber.gouv.fr/alerte/CERTFR-2026-ALE-012/?_sp=d54bf43f-748b-400b-b483-b2335a75e38b.1794001751521) .
